security.event_name: An account was successfully logged on
security.security_meaning: Baseline authentication record: who logged on, from where, using which logon type.
security.triage_priority: Low baseline / High for Logon Type 3 or 10 from an unexpected source
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3 - Lateral Movement (RDP/SMB logons using harvested credentials)
security.example_suspicious_pattern: Logon Type 10 (RDP) to a server from a service account that has never logged on interactively before

security.event_name: An account failed to log on
security.security_meaning: Authentication failure record - the primary brute-force / password-spray signal.
security.triage_priority: High when volume spikes or many distinct accounts fail from one source
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3 - credential stuffing/brute force preceding successful lateral movement
security.example_suspicious_pattern: 10+ failed logons for different target accounts from one source IP within 5 minutes
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4625; group by TargetUserName and IpAddress, count per window

security.event_name: A logon was attempted using explicit credentials
security.security_meaning: A process used alternate, explicitly supplied credentials (runas, mapped drive, PsExec-style tooling).
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3 - Lateral Movement (pass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket tooling using explicit alternate creds)
security.example_suspicious_pattern: A workstation account explicitly authenticating as a Domain Admin to a remote host
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4648; correlate ProcessName with TargetServerName

security.event_name: Special privileges assigned to new logon
security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: Special Logon subcategory (Success) - Advanced Audit Policy
security.security_meaning: An account logged on with admin-equivalent privileges (SeDebugPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, etc.).
security.normal_frequency: Low to medium (should correlate only with documented admins)
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3/6 - flags the exact privileged-logon moment before lateral movement and the GPO ransomware push
security.example_suspicious_pattern: 4672 for an account not on the Task 0 Domain Admins export, or on a workstation that never hosts admin logons
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4672; cross-reference SubjectUserName against domain_baseline.json domainAdmins

security.event_name: A new process has been created
security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: Process Creation subcategory (Success) + command-line auditing registry key (Task 5)
security.security_meaning: Full process execution telemetry, including parent process and (with Task 5's registry key) command line.
security.triage_priority: Medium baseline / High for suspicious binaries or command lines
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3/6 - core telemetry for Mimikatz, PsExec, encoded PowerShell and ransomware binaries
security.example_suspicious_pattern: powershell.exe -enc spawned by winword.exe, or a GPO-deployed scheduled task launching an unsigned binary
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4688; inspect NewProcessName, CommandLine and ParentProcessName

security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: User Account Management subcategory (Success) - Advanced Audit Policy
security.security_meaning: New AD account provisioned - legitimate onboarding or attacker-created persistence.
security.triage_priority: High outside a documented change window
security.crimson_tide_phase: Post-Phase 6 persistence - backup accounts created after the attacker gains Domain Admin
security.example_suspicious_pattern: 4720 with no matching HR onboarding ticket, followed immediately by a 4732 into a privileged group
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4720; correlate SamAccountName against onboarding records

security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: User Account Management subcategory (Success) - Advanced Audit Policy
security.security_meaning: Account removal - routine offboarding or attacker anti-forensic cleanup.
security.triage_priority: Medium baseline / High if paired with a recent 4720 for the same account
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 7 - Extortion/cleanup (removing accounts used during the intrusion)
security.example_suspicious_pattern: 4720 and 4726 for the same account name within a 24-hour window
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4720 and 4726; correlate SamAccountName and time delta

security.event_name: A member was added to a security-enabled local group
security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: Security Group Management subcategory (Success) - Advanced Audit Policy
security.security_meaning: Group membership change - the step immediately after credential theft succeeds in a privilege-escalation chain.
security.triage_priority: Critical when the target group is Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins or G_IT_Admins
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3 - privilege escalation following Kerberoasting/credential theft
security.example_suspicious_pattern: Any addition to Domain Admins/Enterprise Admins/G_IT_Admins with no matching change ticket
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 4732; filter TargetUserName in {Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, G_IT_Admins}

security.audit_or_sensor_dependency: None - always logged by the Security log itself, independent of audit policy
security.security_meaning: The Security event log was cleared - an anti-forensic action, not a configuration option.
security.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 7 - Extortion/cleanup (erasing evidence before or after ransomware detonation)
security.example_suspicious_pattern: Any occurrence at all, especially outside a documented maintenance window
security.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 1102; alert unconditionally, zero acceptable baseline

powershell.security_meaning: Records pipeline execution details and the parameters passed to cmdlets.
powershell.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3/6 - reveals AD/GPO cmdlets (New-GPO, Set-ADAccountControl) run via living-off-the-land PowerShell
powershell.example_suspicious_pattern: Get-ADUser -Filter * piped to an export, or New-GPO invoked outside a documented change ticket

powershell.audit_or_sensor_dependency: PowerShell Script Block Logging (GPO, pending assignment)
powershell.security_meaning: Full de-obfuscated script block text, including scripts assembled dynamically at runtime.
powershell.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3/6 - defeats Base64/obfuscated PowerShell droppers used to stage the GPO ransomware payload
powershell.example_suspicious_pattern: Script blocks containing DownloadString, -enc, IEX, or direct New-GPO/Set-GPRegistryValue calls outside a change ticket

sysmon.security_meaning: Richer process telemetry than 4688: file hash, digital signature status, original filename.
sysmon.triage_priority: Medium baseline / High on hash or signature mismatch
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3/6 - detects unsigned or renamed tooling (renamed PsExec, Mimikatz, GPO-dropped ransomware binary)
sysmon.example_suspicious_pattern: Unsigned binary named svchost.exe running from a path outside System32
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' Id 1; check Hashes and Signed fields

sysmon.triage_priority: Medium baseline / High for unusual destinations
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 4 - Data Exfiltration (Rclone/cloud-storage uploads); Phase 3 SMB/WMI lateral connections
sysmon.example_suspicious_pattern: rclone.exe or powershell.exe making sustained outbound connections to an unrecognized cloud-storage IP range
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 3; filter DestinationIp/DestinationPort against the approved egress list

sysmon.audit_or_sensor_dependency: Sysmon service + image_load rule group (high volume, selectively enabled)
sysmon.security_meaning: DLL/module load events - detects DLL side-loading and reflective injection loaders.
sysmon.normal_frequency: Very high if broadly enabled (usually scoped to sensitive processes)
sysmon.triage_priority: High for unsigned DLLs loaded into lsass.exe or other trusted processes
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 3 - credential-theft tooling (Mimikatz-style DLL injection into lsass.exe)
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 7; filter ImageLoaded targeting lsass.exe with Signed=false

sysmon.security_meaning: File drop telemetry - detects ransomware note drops and staged exfiltration archives.
sysmon.triage_priority: High for known ransomware extensions or mass creation bursts
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 6 - Ransomware Deployment (mass creation of encrypted files and ransom notes)
sysmon.example_suspicious_pattern: Thousands of files with a new extension created across multiple directories in under 60 seconds
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 11; aggregate file-creation rate per process per minute

sysmon.security_meaning: Registry modification telemetry - the primary signal for Run-key and service-based persistence.
sysmon.triage_priority: High for Run/RunOnce key changes by non-installer processes
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Post-Phase 6 persistence - Run-key or service creation to survive reboot after ransomware deployment
sysmon.example_suspicious_pattern: New value under HKLM...\Run pointing to a binary in %TEMP% or %APPDATA%
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 13; filter TargetObject for Run/RunOnce/Services keys

sysmon.security_meaning: Process-level DNS resolution telemetry - detects C2 beaconing and DGA domain lookups.
sysmon.triage_priority: Medium baseline / High for newly-registered or DGA-pattern domains
sysmon.crimson_tide_phase: Phase 1/3 - C2 beaconing following initial access and during lateral movement
sysmon.example_suspicious_pattern: svchost.exe or an Office process resolving a newly-registered, high-entropy domain name
sysmon.validation_method: Get-WinEvent Id 22; cross-reference QueryName against a domain-reputation threat intel feed
